6. When hot iron nail is kept in cold water, the temperature of iron is reduced, whereas temperature of water is increased, why? If a heater with power 1000 W gives 3.6 x 106 Joules of heat energy in one hour. What will be the temperature raised
in the 50 kilogram of water with temperature 30°C by that heat ? (Specific heat capacity of water is 4200 J/kg°C.)
Ans:- When a hot iron nail is placed in cold water, heat flows from the hotter iron to the cooler water. As a result, the iron
loses heat and its temperature decreases, while the water gains heat and its temperature rises, until both reach the same
temperature. This happens because heat naturally transfers from a hotter body to a colder one.
Given mass of water (m) = 50kg
Initial temperature (t1) = 30°C
Final temperature (t) = ?
Specific heat capacity (s) = 4200 J/kg°C Heat energy given (Q) = 3.6 x 106J
Therefore the raised temperature will be 47.14°C.
7. Prove that: Q=msdt
Ans:- The quantity of the heat absorbed by a substance (Q) is directly proportion to its mass (m)
Q ∝ m …………………… i [ keeping the temperature constant ]
The quantity of heat absorbed by a substance (Q) is directly proportional to the change/increase in temperature (𝑇1 − 𝑇2) Q ∝ (𝑇1 − 𝑇2) ……………… ii [keeping the mass constant ]
Combining equation (i) and (ii) then we get
Q ∝ m (𝑇1 − 𝑇2) Or, Q = ms (𝑇1 − 𝑇2) …………….. iii
Where s is a constant and refers to the specific heat capacity of the substance.
Or, Q = msdt ……………. iv where dt= (𝑇1 − 𝑇2)
Therefore, the heat absorbed or released by a substance is equal to the product of the mass (m), the specific heat capacity (s)
and the temperature change (𝑇1 − 𝑇2) of the substance. This equation is called the heat equation. And this is the required
equation.

8. (i) How can we utilize the high specific heat capacity of water for heating our body? Ans:- We can utilize the high specific heat capacity of water to heat our body efficiently because water can store and transfer a lot of heat without a large change in its temperature. For example:

 Hot water bottles or heating pads: Filling a bottle with hot water and placing it on the body releases heat slowly over time, keeping us warm for a long period without the water cooling quickly.  Warm baths or showers: Water in a bath can store a large amount of heat, transferring it to our body gradually, which provides sustained warmth.
